'''Grafana''' is an open-source [[data visualization|analytics and visualization]] [[web application]]. It connects to [[time series database]]s and other data sources, allowing users to build dashboards that display metrics, logs, and traces. Grafana supports data sources including [[Prometheus (software)|Prometheus]], [[Amazon_Elastic_Compute_Cloud#Amazon_CloudWatch|AWS CloudWatch]], [[Graphite (software)|Graphite]], [[InfluxDB]], [[Elasticsearch]], [[PostgreSQL]], and [[MySQL]].<ref name="zdnet">{{Cite web |url=https://www.zdnet.com/article/devops-and-observability-in-the-2020s/ |title=DevOps and observability in the 2020s |last=Anadiotis |first=George |website=ZDNet |access-date=February 4, 2020}}</ref>

Torkel Ödegaard released Grafana in January 2014 as an outgrowth of work on [[Graphite (software)|Graphite]] at [[Orbitz]]. The user interface was originally based on version 3 of [[Kibana]].<ref name="history">{{Cite web |last=Ödegaard |first=Torkel |date=September 3, 2019 |title=The (Mostly) Complete History of Grafana UX |url=https://grafana.com/blog/2019/09/03/the-mostly-complete-history-of-grafana-ux/ |access-date=October 6, 2020 |website=Grafana Labs}}</ref> The company behind the project, initially named Raintank, rebranded as Grafana Labs and has raised over $500 million in venture capital funding, reaching a $6 billion valuation in 2024.<ref name="tc-270m">{{Cite web |last=Lardinois |first=Frederic |date=August 21, 2024 |title=Grafana Labs raises $270M |url=https://techcrunch.com/2024/08/21/grafana-labs-is-now-valued-at-6b/ |access-date=February 25, 2026 |website=TechCrunch}}</ref>

Since 2021, Grafana has been licensed under the [[GNU Affero General Public License|AGPLv3]] (previously [[Apache License|Apache 2.0]]).<ref name="agplv3" /> Grafana Labs provides two commercial Grafana offerings: Grafana Cloud for managed deployments and Grafana Enterprise for self-managed environments. 

Grafana Cloud provides hosted Grafana, managed telemetry services, and additional capabilities such as Adaptive Telemetry for telemetry optimization and Grafana Assistant for AI-assisted observability workflows.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Grafana Cloud documentation {{!}} Grafana Cloud documentation |url=https://grafana.com/docs/grafana-cloud/ |access-date=2026-07-01 |website=Grafana Labs |language=en}}</ref> Grafana Enterprise contains features including LDAP team synchronization, data source permissions, and reporting.<ref name="enterprise">{{Cite web |title=Grafana Enterprise Stack |work=Grafana Labs |access-date=March 19, 2021 |url=https://grafana.com/products/enterprise/}}</ref>

== History ==
Grafana was first released in January 2014, initially targeting Graphite and InfluxDB as data sources. It later added support for relational databases including MySQL, PostgreSQL, and [[Microsoft SQL Server]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=MySQL data source |url=https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/datasources/mysql/ |access-date=April 23, 2024 |website=Grafana Labs}}</ref>

Grafana Labs was founded in 2014 as Raintank and later adopted the name, Grafana, which combines Graphite and Kibana.<ref name="story">{{Cite web |title='The Story of Grafana' documentary: The business of open source |url=https://grafana.com/blog/the-story-of-grafana-documentary-the-business-of-open-source/ |access-date=February 25, 2026 |website=Grafana Labs}}</ref> The company raised $24 million in Series A funding in 2019,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.zdnet.com/article/is-open-source-the-way-to-go-for-observability-grafana-labs-scores-24m-series-a-funding-to-try-to-prove-this/ |title=Grafana Labs scores $24M Series A funding |last=Anadiotis |first=George |website=ZDNet |access-date=February 4, 2020}}</ref> $50 million in Series B in 2020,<ref>{{Cite press release |last=Grafana |date=August 17, 2020 |title=Grafana Labs Raises $50 Million |url=https://www.globenewswire.com/en/news-release/2020/08/17/2079144/0/en/Grafana-Labs-Raises-50-Million-to-Accelerate-R-D-Investments-in-Open-Source-Logs-Metrics-and-Composable-Observability.html |access-date=July 23, 2021 |website=GlobeNewswire}}</ref> $220 million in Series C in 2021 (at a $3 billion valuation),<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 24, 2021 |title=Grafana Labs Raises $220 Million Round at $3 Billion Valuation |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-08-24/grafana-labs-raises-220-million-round-at-3-billion-valuation |access-date=August 22, 2021 |website=Bloomberg}}</ref> and $270 million in 2024 at a $6 billion valuation.<ref name="tc-270m" />

== Architecture ==
Grafana's backend is written in [[Go (programming language)|Go]] and its frontend in [[TypeScript]] using [[React (JavaScript library)|React]].<ref name="openhub" /> The application runs as a single binary that serves a web interface and connects to external data sources through a plugin system. Plugins fall into three categories: data source plugins (for querying backends), panel plugins (for visualization types), and app plugins (for bundled functionality).<ref name="enterprise" />

Grafana does not store the metrics, logs, or traces it visualizes; it queries external data sources when a dashboard is rendered and can combine results from several sources in a single panel. It maintains its own relational database (SQLite by default, or MySQL or PostgreSQL) for dashboards, users, annotations and alert state.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Data sources {{!}} Grafana documentation |url=https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/datasources/ |access-date=2026-09-22 |website=Grafana Labs |language=en}}</ref> Core data sources shipped with Grafana include [[Prometheus (software)|Prometheus]], [[Graphite (software)|Graphite]], [[InfluxDB]] and OpenTSDB for metrics; Loki and Elasticsearch for logs; Tempo, Jaeger and Zipkin for traces; Pyroscope and Parca for profiles; and [[MySQL]], PostgreSQL and Microsoft SQL Server. Other backends, including [[OpenSearch (software)|OpenSearch]] and [[Splunk]], are available as separately installed plugins. 

Dashboards are defined as JSON documents and can be provisioned from files, version-controlled, and shared via Grafana's public dashboard library. Alerting rules can be defined against any data source, with notifications routed to email, [[Slack (software)|Slack]], [[PagerDuty]], and other channels.<ref name="enterprise" />

== LGTM Stack ==
Grafana Labs develops a set of open-source backends that are often deployed together as the "LGTM Stack" (Loki, Grafana, Tempo, Mimir):<ref name="lgtm">{{Cite web |last=Nerkar |first=Prashant |date=March 28, 2024 |title=Building an Open Source Observability Platform |url=https://devops.com/building-an-open-source-observability-platform/ |access-date=February 25, 2026 |website=DevOps.com}}</ref>

* '''Loki:''' A horizontally scalable, highly available, multi-tenant log aggregation system inspired by Prometheus.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Get started with Grafana Loki {{!}} Grafana Loki documentation |url=https://grafana.com/docs/loki/latest/get-started/ |access-date=2026-07-16 |website=Grafana Labs |language=en}}</ref> Loki indexes metadata rather than the full text of the log lines. The Loki project started at Grafana Labs in 2018 and is released under the AGPLv3 license.<ref>{{cite web |last=Lobo |first=Savia |title=Grafana Labs announces general availability of Loki 1.0 |url=https://hub.packtpub.com/grafana-labs-announces-general-availability-of-loki-1-0-a-multi-tenant-log-aggregation-system/ |website=Packt Hub |access-date=April 19, 2023 |date=November 20, 2019}}</ref>
* '''Mimir:''' A horizontally scalable, highly available, multi-tenant time-series database for long-term storage of Prometheus metrics. The Mimir project was announced by Grafana Labs in 2022 as a replacement for Cortex and is released under the AGPLv3 license.<ref>{{cite web |last=Gain |first=B. Cameron |title=The Great Grafana Mimir and Cortex Split |url=https://thenewstack.io/the-great-grafana-mimir-and-cortex-split/ |website=The New Stack |access-date=April 19, 2023 |date=August 10, 2022}}</ref> 
* '''Tempo:''' A high-scale distributed tracing database that requires only object storage to operate and does not index trace data. Tempo can ingest common open source tracing protocols, including Jaeger, Zipkin and OpenTelemetry. The Tempo project was announced by Grafana Labs in 2020 and is released under the AGPLv3 license.<ref>{{cite web |last=Deutscher |first=Maria |title=Grafana Labs eases IT monitoring with Tempo tracing tool |url=https://siliconangle.com/2021/06/08/grafana-labs-eases-monitoring-tempo-tracing-tool-new-grafana-release/ |website=SiliconANGLE |access-date=April 19, 2023 |date=June 8, 2021}}</ref>
* '''Pyroscope:''' A highly available, multi-tenant continuous profiling database for storing and querying profiling data at scale. Pyroscope integrates natively with Grafana to correlate profiles with metrics, logs and traces. The Pyroscope project was announced by Grafana Labs in 2023 and is released under the AGPLv3 license.<ref>{{cite web |last=Vizard |first=Mike |title=Grafana Labs Delivers Open Source Code Profiling Tool |url=https://devops.com/grafana-labs-delivers-open-source-code-profiling-tool/ |website=DevOps.com |access-date=May 27, 2024 |date=August 31, 2023}}</ref>

== Other open source projects ==
In addition to the LGTM Stack, Grafana Labs, has developed additional open-source projects:

* '''Alloy:''' A vendor-neutral distribution of the OpenTelemetry Collector, offering native pipelines for OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Loki, Tempo, and Pyroscope telemetry formats to collect metrics, logs, traces, and profiles. Alloy replaced Grafana Agent, which entered long-term support in 2024 and reached end-of-life in November 2025. The Alloy project was announced by Grafana Labs at GrafanaCON in 2024 and is released under the Apache 2.0 license.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barron |first=Jenna |date=2024-04-09 |title=Grafana Labs releases Grafana 11, Loki 3.0, and a new open source project called Grafana Alloy |url=https://sdtimes.com/grafana/grafana-labs-releases-grafana-11-loki-3-0-and-a-new-open-source-project-called-grafana-alloy/ |access-date=2026-09-14 |website=SD Times |language=en-US}}</ref>
* '''Beyla:''' An eBPF-based automatic instrumentation tool that captures RED (rate, error, duration) metrics and trace spans for Linux HTTP/S and gRPC services without modifying application code. Beyla supports applications written in Go, C/C++, Rust, Python, Ruby, Java, Node.js, and .NET. The Beyla project was started at Grafana Labs and announced in 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wheatley |first=Mike |date=2023-11-14 |title=Grafana Labs acquires AI startup Asserts.ai to ease application observability headaches |url=https://siliconangle.com/2023/11/14/grafana-labs-acquires-ai-startup-asserts-ai-ease-application-observability-headaches/ |access-date=2026-09-14 |website=SiliconANGLE |language=en-US}}</ref> It was donated to the OpenTelemetry project in 2025 as OpenTelemetry eBPF Instrumentation, <ref>{{Cite web |last=Grcevski |first=Nikola |last2=Yahn{{!}} |first2=Tyler |date=2025-11-03 |title=OpenTelemetry eBPF Instrumentation Marks the First Release |url=https://opentelemetry.io/blog/2025/obi-announcing-first-release/ |access-date=2026-09-14 |website=OpenTelemetry |language=en}}</ref> and is released under the Apache 2.0 license. 
* '''Faro:''' A web SDK for real user monitoring (RUM) that instruments browser-based frontend applications to capture performance metrics, logs, exceptions, user events, and traces. Faro data can be correlated with backend and infrastructure telemetry in the LGTM stack for full-stack observability. The Faro project was announced by Grafana Labs in 2022 and is released under the Apache 2.0 license.<ref>{{Citation |title=grafana/faro-web-sdk |date=2026-09-14 |url=https://github.com/grafana/faro-web-sdk |access-date=2026-09-14 |publisher=Grafana Labs}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Grafana Releases New Frontend Observability SDK and Backend Profiling Database |url=https://www.infoq.com/news/2022/12/grafana-faro-phlare/ |access-date=2026-09-14 |website=InfoQ |language=en}}</ref>
* '''[[K6 (software)|k6]]:''' Load and performance testing tool that uses test scripts written in JavaScript or TypeScript to help identify and fix performance issues before they reach production. The k6 project was started in 2016 as LoadImpact and was acquired by Grafana Labs in 2021, and is released under the AGPLv3 license.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Vizard |first=Mike |date=2021-06-17 |title=Grafana Labs Acquires k6 to Add Open Source Load Testing Tool |url=https://devops.com/grafana-labs-acquires-k6-to-add-open-source-load-testing-tool/ |access-date=2026-09-14 |website=DevOps.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Adoption ==
Grafana is used by [[Wikimedia]]'s infrastructure,<ref>{{Cite web |title=grafana.wikimedia.org |url=https://wikitech.wikimedia.org/wiki/Grafana.wikimedia.org |work=Wikitech |access-date=April 9, 2021}}</ref> [[NASA]] and the [[Tour de France]] (for real-time race telemetry).<ref name="forbes">{{Cite web |last=Nieva |first=Richard |date=September 30, 2025 |title=Grafana Labs Is Cleaning Up On The Vibe Coding Boom |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/richardnieva/2025/09/30/grafana-labs-revenue-tender-offer/ |website=Forbes}}</ref> As of 2026, Grafana Labs has more than 10,000 paying customers, <ref>{{Cite web |last=Weiss |first=Geoff |title=Grafana Labs' $600 million milestone points to AI's next phase |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/grafana-labs-arr-600-million-ai-demand-2026-8 |access-date=2026-09-03 |website=Business Insider |language=en-US}}</ref> including [[Nvidia]], [[Anthropic]] and [[Uber]].<ref name="forbes" />
